criteria.rationale: Examined the B35 gate (roadmap :77-81) against the code and the measurements. Identity is checked at handshake and on every hosted request before the handler (runtime.go:426,449-456); the peer UID is checked before any read (runtime.go:404-408); admission refuses on a full lane or at the deadline (runtime_host.go:107-119); the fourth measurement run passes T1-T7 with RAM, CPU and latency per scenario. The departures (no watcher, so the memo is keyed by commit; no retry of hosted reads; no CPU quota or per-command limits) are disclosed in the ADR amendment at line 271 and in the roadmap. Concluded that the gate has falsifiable evidence.

The runtime, resident-cache and QoS slices compose through one Handler/Busy/Metrics contract in worktreeruntime.Options, and the sealed integration evidence for all three passes (optional-worktree-runtime, resident-cache, runtime-qos).

All three ordered member specs are status: done with no unchecked tasks. The crit:medium follow-up of the resident-cache spec is marked covered by the qos spec. The delivery code is unchanged since the round-4 approval, so the closures remain current.
Examined the sealed module validation of pose-mcp: the unit, build and every integration and reachability check pass. Concluded there is no regression.

The cross-spec items not delivered (CPU quota/affinity, per-command limits, Windows named pipe, default routing) are in their own draft specs, per the roadmap (:18-20) and the ADR (:301). The only open items are R3-N4 and R3-N5, which are low and remain the follow-ups accepted in round 4.
